Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: Electoral register uses national identification number (NIN) as unique identifier with 100% completeness, and is linked to biometric ID processes.
revision_notes: Original cena.sn PDF link is dead (SOURCE_NOT_AVAILABLE); located an accessible mirror of the same 2021 MAFE electoral file audit report (the 'Rapport Final MAFE 2021 du Sénégal'). The audit confirms the national identification number (NIN) field has 100% completeness in the electoral register and serves as each elector's unique identifier, captured jointly with the biometric ECOWAS identity card (CNI) which doubles as the voter card, per Decree n°2016-1536. Score confirmed at 5 (Fully integrated nationwide).
revised_comments: Senegal's electoral register is a biometric file in which the national identification number (NIN) serves as each voter's unique identifier, achieving 100% completeness across the register. NIN and biometric data (fingerprints and photograph) are captured through the same enrolment process as the ECOWAS biometric national identity card (Carte Nationale d'Identité biométrique CEDEAO), managed by the Direction de l'Automatisation des Fichiers, and this card doubles as the voter card, giving the electoral register full technical integration with the national identification system nationwide.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the government's national data exchange system?
Comments: World Bank project documentation notes lack of integrated land information systems (SGF national and municipal SIF/LIS) and that interoperability is being clarified; indicates partial/ongoing data exchange capability rather than mature national interoperability.
revision_notes: Original score (2, Planned) rested on a 2021 Project Information Document noting interoperability was still being 'clarified'. A November 2025 PROCASEF World Bank supervision mission report confirms active technical work defining SGF-SIFCOM interoperability requirements ('besoins d'interopérabilité, à traduire ensuite en fonctionnalités à développer'), and Senegal's national government interoperability platform (Plateforme d'Interopérabilité/Jokkoo, X-Road based) has been in pilot phase since April 2025 with full national rollout targeted for 2025-2027. No source confirms the land register is yet live on this national exchange platform, so 'partially integrated' cannot be asserted, but 'planned' understates the concrete technical work now under way. Recalculated to 3 (Under development).
revised_comments: Senegal's land register is not yet connected to the government's national data exchange system, but concrete technical work towards interoperability is under way. The Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines is developing a Système de Gestion Foncière (SGF) intended to interoperate with the PROCASEF-built Système d'Information Foncière Communal (SIFCOM), with interoperability requirements defined and being translated into system functionality as of late 2025. Separately, Senegal launched a national government interoperability platform (Plateforme d'Interopérabilité/Jokkoo, built on X-Road) in April 2025, currently in pilot phase with full national rollout planned for 2025-2027; land administration systems are not yet confirmed as connected to this platform.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: Senegal has a National Single Registry (RNU) institutionalized by Decree No. 2021-1052 (Aug 2, 2021) for poor/vulnerable households.
revision_notes: Original score (4, Partially deployed) rested on the 2021 institutionalising decree alone. Fuller evidence shows the RNU's management information system, built with ADIE (now Sénégal Numérique), has operated across all 14 regions of Senegal since its 2018-2021 update, with household coverage having grown from roughly 541,000 (29% of households) to about one million households by 2024 (DGPSN, December 2025). The register's institutional and technical infrastructure is therefore deployed nationwide, even though beneficiary coverage itself (captured separately under Uptake) remains partial. Recalculated to 5 (Fully deployed nationwide). Flagged for human review as this reaches the top of the scale.
revised_comments: Senegal maintains a National Single Registry (Registre National Unique, RNU), a digital social protection register operated nationwide across all 14 regions by the Délégation Générale à la Protection Sociale et à la Solidarité Nationale (DGPSN), with its management information system hosted and developed by the state digital agency (ADIE/Sénégal Numérique). Household coverage has grown from around 541,000 households (29% of all households) following the 2018-2021 update to approximately one million households by 2024, as the register has been extended beyond the extreme poor to include households vulnerable to climate and economic shocks.
